In October 1962, modifications had just been completed in JPL's Space Flight Operations Center, located in Building 125, in preparation for the launch of Ranger 5.
This facility became obsolete after the construction of the larger and more technologically advanced Space Flight Operations Facility (SFOF) in building 230, which opened in May 1964.

70788057.title: File:U.S. Ambassador and Power Information Technology Company CEO Commemorate Opening of Network Operations Center in Lahore (15239120339).jpg

ObjectName.value: U.S. Ambassador and Power Information Technology Company CEO Commemorate Opening of Network Operations Center in Lahore (15239120339)

Categories.value: PD USAID|Images with annotations|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Richard Olson (diplomat)|USGov images uploaded by Hiàn|Images from USAID Pakistan

ImageDescription.value: Lahore, October 2, 2014 -- Ambassador Richard Olson and Power Information Technology Company CEO, Hassan Bukhari led an inauguration ceremony at the Network Operations Center at the Lahore Water and Power Development Authority Office on Thursday.  The facility was established through a partnership between Pakistan’s electricity distribution companies and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).  It will serve to alleviate Pakistan’s continuing energy crisis by allowing more effective management of available electricity and reducing unscheduled load shedding throughout Pakistan.  The Center manages new state-of-the-art monitoring and control systems that have been installed in all ten government-owned power distribution companies (DISCOs), which will more efficiently allocate Pakistan’s electricity.

Credit.value: U.S. Ambassador and Power Information Technology Company CEO Commemorate Opening of Network Operations Center in Lahore

195284636.title: File:Watching Over the Deep Space Network Before Artemis II Signal Acquisition.jpg

ObjectName.value: Watching Over the Deep Space Network Before Artemis II Signal Acquisition

Categories.value: PD NASA|Deep Space Network|Artemis 2|United States photographs taken on 2026-04-01|NASA Website files uploaded by OptimusPrimeBot

ImageDescription.value: Blanca Renteria, Artemis Deep Space Network (DSN) operations chief, monitors data at the Space Flight Operations Facility at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California shortly after Artemis II launched from the agency’s Kennedy Space Flight Center in Florida on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT. The Space Flight Operations Facility operates the DSN, which comprises three complexes in Goldstone, California; Madrid, Spain; and Canberra, Australia. Each complex consists of several radio frequency antennas that communicate with dozens of robotic spacecraft exploring the solar system in addition to the crewed Artemis II mission. The DSN is managed by JPL for the agency’s Space Communications and Navigation program, which is located at NASA Headquarters within the Space Operations Mission Directorate. The DSN allows missions to track, send commands to, and receive scientific data from faraway spacecraft. JPL is managed by Caltech in Pasadena, California, for NASA.

Credit.value: Watching Over the Deep Space Network Before Artemis II Signal Acquisition
